# Participants & scoring

Invite and manage people, review their answers, score by rubric, and show the ranking.

[ParticipantTable](#participanttable) · [ParticipantDrawer](#participantdrawer) · [InviteDialog](#invitedialog) · [SubmissionReview](#submissionreview) · [RubricScorer](#rubricscorer) · [Leaderboard](#leaderboard) · [Podium](#podium) · [ScoreHeatGrid](#scoreheatgrid)

### ParticipantTable

Everyone in the contest in a searchable, sortable table: status, team, how far they got and their score. Tick rows to message them together.

```ts
import { ParticipantTable } from '@/contest/components/ParticipantTable'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `participants` *(required)* | `Participant[]` |  | The people. |
| `submissions` | `Submission[]` |  | Adds the answers and score columns. |
| `onOpen` *(required)* | `(participant: Participant) => void` |  | Called when a name is clicked. |
| `selectedId` | `string \| null` |  | The person open in the drawer; the name is highlighted. |
| `onInvite` | `() => void` |  | Shows an "Invite people" button. |
| `onMessage` | `(people: Participant[]) => void` |  | Shows a "Message them" button when rows are ticked. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<ParticipantTable participants={people} submissions={submissions} onOpen={(p) => setOpenId(p.id)} onInvite={() => setInviting(true)} />
```

- It is the kit `DataGrid`, so sorting, resizing, density and column visibility come with it. Ticked rows are reported through `onCheckedChange`.

### ParticipantDrawer

One person in a side sheet: status, a note, what they did and when, their score and rank, and a link to their answers.

```ts
import { ParticipantDrawer } from '@/contest/components/ParticipantDrawer'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `participant` *(required)* | `Participant \| null` |  | The person to show. The drawer is open while this is set. |
| `submission` | `Submission` |  | Their submission, for the score and the timeline. |
| `rank` | `number` |  | Their place on the leaderboard, when they have one. |
| `onClose` *(required)* | `() => void` |  | Called when the drawer is closed. |
| `onSave` *(required)* | `(participant: Participant) => void` |  | Called with the changed person. |
| `onReview` | `(submission: Submission) => void` |  | Shows a "Review the answers" button. |
| `now` | `Date` |  | Replaces the clock, for tests and demos. |

```tsx
<ParticipantDrawer participant={open} submission={sub} rank={rank} onClose={() => setOpenId(null)} onSave={(p) => void people.save(p)} />
```

- Changing the status to "disqualified" asks first. A disqualified person leaves the leaderboard and every audience.
- Edits stay in a draft until "Save changes".

### InviteDialog

Paste a list of people and invite them in one go. The list is read as you type, and every line that is wrong says why.

```ts
import { InviteDialog } from '@/contest/components/InviteDialog'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` *(required)* | `boolean` |  | Shows the dialog. |
| `onClose` *(required)* | `() => void` |  | Called when the dialog is cancelled or finished. |
| `existingEmails` | `string[]` |  | Addresses already in the contest, so a repeat is caught before it is sent. |
| `onInvite` *(required)* | `(people: InvitePerson[]) => void \| Promise<void>` |  | Called with the lines that read fine. The dialog closes after it finishes. |

```tsx
<InviteDialog open={inviting} onClose={() => setInviting(false)} existingEmails={people.map((p) => p.email)} onInvite={(list) => people.invite(list)} />
```

- Accepted lines: `ada@example.com`, `Ada Lindqvist <ada@example.com>, Comets`, `Ada Lindqvist, ada@example.com, Comets`. See `parseInvites`.

### SubmissionReview

Look at what a participant answered next to the answer key, see the points the key gave and why, and change them. Written answers and photos are scored with the rubric.

```ts
import { SubmissionReview } from '@/contest/components/SubmissionReview'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `questions` *(required)* | `Question[]` |  | The questions of the submission, in order. |
| `submission` *(required)* | `Submission` |  | The submission to review. |
| `answerKeys` *(required)* | `Record<string, AnswerKey>` |  | The answer keys by question id. |
| `participantName` | `string` |  | Shown in the heading. |
| `media` | `(id: string) => MediaAsset \| undefined` |  | Looks up uploaded files, to show the photo that was answered. |
| `onScore` *(required)* | `(questionId: string, score: Score) => void` |  | Called with the score the reviewer saved. The review then moves to the next answer that needs a person. |
| `initialQuestionId` | `string` |  | Opens this question first, instead of the first answer that is waiting. |
| `reviewer` | `string` | `'Reviewer'` | Written into every score saved here. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<SubmissionReview
  key={submission.id}
  questions={questions}
  submission={submission}
  answerKeys={keys}
  participantName="Bo Tanaka"
  onScore={(qid, score) => void submissions.saveScore(submission.id, qid, score)}
/>
```

- A score saved here is `auto: false` and carries the reviewer and the note. "Use the key's score" puts the automatic score back.
- `Ctrl+Enter` (`⌘+Enter` on a Mac) saves from anywhere in the scoring box.
- The question map colours each answer: waiting for a person, scored by the key, or scored by a reviewer.

### RubricScorer

Score an answer by criteria: one slider per criterion, with a running total.

```ts
import { RubricScorer } from '@/contest/components/RubricScorer'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rubric` *(required)* | `RubricCriterion[]` |  | The criteria from the answer key. |
| `value` *(required)* | `Record<string, number>` |  | Points per criterion, by id. A criterion that is missing counts as 0. |
| `onChange` *(required)* | `(value: Record<string, number>) => void` |  | Called with the new points. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Locks the sliders. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<RubricScorer rubric={key.rubric} value={points} onChange={setPoints} />
```

- Keyboard: arrow keys change the points by one, Page Up and Page Down in larger steps, Home and End jump to 0 and to the full points. "Full marks" and "Zero" set every criterion at once.

### Leaderboard

The ranking as a list: place with medal colours, name, a bar for the points, and an arrow for the places gained or lost. When the order changes, the rows slide to their new places.

```ts
import { Leaderboard } from '@/contest/components/Leaderboard'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` *(required)* | `RankedRow[]` |  | The ranking, best first. See `rankParticipants`. |
| `teams` | `TeamRow[]` |  | Adds a People / Teams switch. See `rankTeams`. |
| `highlightId` | `string` |  | The row of the person looking at the board: highlighted and tagged "You". |
| `changes` | `Record<string, number>` |  | Places moved since the last ranking, by id: positive is up. See `rankChanges`. |
| `limit` | `number` |  | Shows only the best N rows. |
| `onOpen` | `(row: RankedRow) => void` |  | Makes a row clickable. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
const ranked = rankParticipants(people, submissions)
const { rows, changes } = useRankReplay(ranked, 'public')

<Leaderboard rows={rows} teams={rankTeams(ranked)} highlightId={me.id} changes={changes} />
```

- Ties share a place and the next place is skipped (1, 2, 2, 4). "+?" next to the points means some answers still wait for a reviewer.
- The slide uses `useFlip`, which skips the motion for people who prefer reduced motion.

### Podium

The first three of a ranking on a podium: first in the middle and tallest, second on the left, third on the right.

```ts
import { Podium } from '@/contest/components/Podium'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` *(required)* | `RankedRow[]` |  | The ranking, best first. Only the first three are shown. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<Podium rows={rankParticipants(people, submissions)} />
```

### ScoreHeatGrid

Who got what: a person on every row, a question in every column, each cell coloured by the share of the points it earned. The hardest question is tagged.

```ts
import { ScoreHeatGrid } from '@/contest/components/ScoreHeatGrid'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `questions` *(required)* | `Question[]` |  | One column each, in order. |
| `rows` *(required)* | `Array<{ id: string; name: string; scores: Record<string, Score \| undefined> }>` |  | One row per person, with their scores by question id. |
| `onOpen` | `(participantId: string, questionId: string) => void` |  | Makes a scored cell clickable, to open that answer. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<ScoreHeatGrid questions={asked} rows={ranked.map((r) => ({ id: r.id, name: r.name, scores: subOf(r.id).scores }))} onOpen={openAnswer} />
```

- Answers that wait for a reviewer are hatched and are left out of "hardest". The bottom row shows the share of people with full marks on each question.
